# misroute

> Finds the tools an agent confuses on an MCP server or OpenAPI spec, tests whether a description change helps against a neutral baseline on held out requests, and writes better descriptions for review.

Install with `pip install misroute` or `uv tool install misroute`. `misroute guide` prints the agent guide (AGENTS.md) and this reference. misroute never edits tools.

## Commands

- `misroute quick [target] [--from claude|cursor|vscode|path] [--server NAME] [--model provider:model] [--demo] [--config-only] --json --max-cost N --no-open`: write misroute.yaml when there is none, then lint and a capped discover. `--config-only` stops after writing the config
- `misroute doctor --json`: setup checks with a fix per problem
- `misroute lint [--draft] [--strict] [--sarif file] --json`: weak descriptions, free
- `misroute discover [--pilot] [--probe] [--pair a,b] --json --max-cost N`: ranked confused tool pairs from model behaviour. `--pilot` runs 3 real trials per model and mode before the estimate. `--probe` then tests the flagged pairs with harder requests, `--pair` the named pairs, and the result gains `probe`
- `misroute check --tool NAME --description TEXT --json --max-cost N [--refresh]`: is a proposed description better
- `misroute check --pair a,b | --flagged [--top N] [--trials 96] --json --max-cost N`: draft a boundary clause for the pair and test it against the original and a neutral edit
- `misroute improve [target] [--model M] [--helper H] [--languages no,en] [--fastmcp] [--out dir] --json --max-cost N`: write, race and confirm new descriptions for confused tools, export for review. Advanced: `--domain`, `--real-requests`, `--requests-from interface|descriptions`, `--max-groups` (default every flagged group), `--styles boundary,returns,example,minimal`, `--max-chars` (no cut by default), `--modes`, `--no-drafts`
- `misroute compare --from OLD --to NEW [--modes json] [--pilot] --json --max-cost N`: does routing change between two models, on the same requests
- `misroute ci [--changed --baseline tools.json --markdown out.md] --json`: limits or changed tools only. `misroute ci --snapshot`: tool names, hashes and descriptions as JSON for `--baseline`, free
- `misroute report [--output file]`: HTML report. `misroute report --pair a,b --json`: misrouted requests between two tools and what the model called. `misroute report --site name=workdir`: static site. All free
- `misroute requests collect [--from log.jsonl] [--file real.jsonl] --json`: candidates from a guard log or trace, `misroute requests review`: a person confirms each in a terminal, `misroute requests status --json`: counts per tool
- `misroute serve mcp|ui|guard -c misroute.yaml`: misroute as an MCP server, the web interface, or a guard proxy. `misroute serve guard --approve ID` approves a held call
- `misroute guide [--schema NAME]`: this reference and the agent guide, or one JSON Schema: lint, discover, check, check_pair, compare, improve, report_pair, doctor, estimate, error

Folded in, they answer with the new form and exit 3: `init`, `probe`, `fix`, `explain`, `site`, `schema`, `ui`, `guard`. `serve-mcp` and `catalog` still run.

Shared flags: `--json`, `--yes`, `--max-cost DOLLARS`, `--estimate-only`, `--progress bar|ndjson|none`, `-c misroute.yaml`.

Targets: MCP URL, local command, OpenAPI or Swagger file, tool list in MCP, OpenAI or Anthropic format, or an MCP client config.

Models: `provider:model` shorthand with providers anthropic, foundry, bedrock, azure, openai, openrouter, ollama, vllm, lmstudio. Prices are looked up automatically, local models are free, and a model with no known price refuses paid runs until `price_in` and `price_out` are set. A model block with `options: {api: responses, reasoning_effort: low}` uses the Responses API. Set a helper model from another family for writing and judging requests (`--helper`, or `generator`, `validator`, `writer` in misroute.yaml).

Config keys: `server` (`url`, `command`, `openapi` or `tools`, plus `name`, `include_tools`, `exclude_tools`, `headers`, `env`), or `servers`, a list of them loaded into one catalog, `system_prompt` (the agent's own, text or a file), `models`, `generator`, `validator`, `writer`, `modes`, `budget_usd`, `requests_per_tool`, `slots`, `rotations`, `repeats`, `max_turns`, `request_source` (`description` or `spec`), `request_languages`, `domain`, `real_requests`, `lookup_tools` (names or patterns of entry point tools not scored as choices), `fixtures` (file of recorded results per tool), `system_certs`, `limits`, `guard`.

## Exit codes

0 passed, 1 limits failed or worse, 2 insufficient data, 3 budget, cost cap, provider or config problem.

## JSON

Every `--json` output is one object with `schema_version` (currently 2) and `command`. Errors have `error` and `exit_code`, and a stop during a run also has `spent`. An estimate has `estimate.calls` and `estimate.cost_usd`, a guide rather than an upper bound, since `--max-cost` and `budget_usd` are what limit spend. Paid runs carry it in their result, with `estimate.above_max_cost` when it was above the cap, which warns and does not refuse. Results with a `roles_warning` list used a helper model from the same family as a tested model.

Template test fields, used by check, fix and improve: `templates`, `discordant_templates`, `p` (exact sign flip over request templates), `p_trial_midp` (trial level, reported only), `fixed`, `broke`, `diff` (error rate change), `ci` (95% interval of diff). Fewer than 6 discordant templates means no verdict.

`check` returns: `tool`, `neighbours`, `verdict` (`better`, `worse`, `no_difference`, `insufficient_data`), `reason`, `baseline_kind` (`neutral` or `description`), `baseline`, the template test fields, `wrong_rate` and `hedge_rate` per condition (`current`, `baseline`, `proposed`) on held out requests, `leakage`, `trials`, `held_out`, `vs_current`, `looks` (verdicts this held out set has given, p is multiplied by it), `round`, `cost_usd`, `roles_warning`, plus `tuning` and `held_out` blocks.

`report --pair` returns: `pair`, `directions` (per direction: `trials`, `wrong`, `hedge`, `examples` with `request`, `called`, `model`, `mode`, `kind`).

`discover` returns: `cells` (per model and mode: `trials`, `accuracy` (first choice right), `decided` (trials where a choice was seen) and `accuracy_decided` (right among those), `unread_pages_rate` (code programs that left later pages unread, not a failure), `reached_rate` (target called within `max_turns`), `wrong_rate` (another tool and never the target in the deciding turn), `hedge_rate`, `write_hedge_rate`, `failures` (including `read_first` and `lookup_only`, where the choice was not seen), `bad_args_rate` and `bad_args` (calls that break the tool's input schema, apart from the tool choice), `unanswered`, `matrix`), `spots` (`a`, `b`, `score` (the larger of the wrong and hedge rates), `ci95` (Wilson 95% interval for the signal behind the score, counting request templates), `signals`, `errors` (most wrong or hedged requests in one model and mode), `templates` (distinct request templates behind them), `flagged` (errors at least 6 over at least 2 templates), `one_wording` (6 errors from a single template, not flagged), `directions`, `write`, `thin`, `cross_server`), `unrouted` (per tool: `rate`, `count`, `trials`, `where`, `example`, requests that ended with no tool call, ranked with the spots), `near_misses`, `removal`, `noise`, `short`, `rejected_requests` (per tool: `request`, `picked`, `reason` for each request the validator dropped), `untested`, `lookup_tools`, `lookup_candidates` (`tool`, `trials`, `targets`: tools called on the way to several targets), `max_turns`, `thin_interface` (tools with no output schema under `request_source: spec`, where the helper cannot tell what a tool returns), `request_use` (`written`, `reused`: tools whose requests were written in this run or reused from an earlier one under the same instructions, domain, source and languages), `servers` (tool to server, with several servers), `system_prompt` (whether the agent's own prompt was used), `pilot` (with `--pilot`: `trials`, `cost_usd`), `usage` (per model: `roles`, `calls`, `cached`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `reasoning_tokens` (the part of `tokens_out` spent on reasoning, where the provider reports it), `cost_usd`), `effect_unknown` (tools with no read or write annotation and no telling verb, also in `lint`, which count as reads), `request_source`, `by_language` and `by_kind` (rates per request language and per kind `goal`, `borrowed`, `real`), `roles_warning`, `spent`, and with `--probe` or `--pair` a `probe` block (`rows` per pair, model and mode: `directions`, `borrowed_wrong`, `goal_wrong`, `real_wrong`, `gate_p`).

`compare` returns: `from`, `to`, `verdict` (the least favourable over modes), `modes` (per mode: `verdict`, `reason`, the template test fields with `diff` as the error rate of `to` minus `from`, `rates` per model with `accuracy`, `reached_rate`, `wrong_rate`, `hedge_rate`, `bad_args_rate`, `tools` with `errors_from` and `errors_to`, `pairs` with `new`, `gone`, `both`), `templates`, `by_kind`, `cost_usd`, `usage`.

`requests collect` and `requests status` return: `file`, `added`, `requests`, `reviewed`, `pending`, `per_tool`, `tools_without`.

`check --pair` returns: `verdict` (over all pairs), `pairs` (`pair`, `model`, `mode`, `baseline_kind`, `errors` for `original`, `baseline`, `clause`, the template test fields, `vs_original` (the same test of clause against the original description, the deploy comparison), `p_holm`, `hedge_p`, `verdict`, `directions`, `leakage`, `edits` with `host_ratio`), `across` and `roles_warning`. Verdicts: `deploy` needs the clause to beat the baseline and the original; beating only the baseline reads `do not deploy`, the content matters but the clause adds nothing over the current text.

`improve` returns: `audit` (`tools`, `reads`, `writes`, `counts`, `notes` with `tool`, `kind` (`description`, `name`, `hint`, `exclude`, `overlap`, `upload`, `binary`, `header`, `spec`), `detail`), `groups` (`tools`, `requests`, `original`, `baseline`, `winner`, `style`, `candidates`, `dropped`, `race`, `confirm` with `rates` per condition (with `real_error_rate` when real requests are held out), `tests` for `winner_vs_baseline`, `winner_vs_original` and `baseline_vs_original` with `verdict`, `reason`, `p_holm` and the template test fields, and `by_language`, then `export` (`winner`, `baseline` or `original`) and `why`), `entries` (`tool`, `op_id`, `route`, `description`, `original`, `status` (`tested`, `tested baseline`, `kept`, `draft`, `unchanged`), `reason`, `read_only`, `destructive`, `suggest_exclude`, `notes`, and `review` with `decision` (`accept`, `reject`, `edit`, `pending`), `exclude` and `by` once a person reviewed it in `misroute ui`), `files`, `fastmcp` (`ok`, `tools`, `missing`, `descriptions_differ`, `hints_differ`, `arguments_differ`, `held_out`), `cost_usd`, `usage`.

## MCP tools

`lint_descriptions`, `draft_description`, `estimate_check`, `check_description`, `explain_pair`, `suggest_fix`, `get_report`, `start_job` (kind `discover`, `probe`, `fix` or `improve`, required `max_cost`, `estimate_only`, `args`). Paid tools require `max_cost`, `job_status`, `cancel_job`. Resource `misroute://guide` holds this text.

## Rules

misroute never edits tools. Drafts are for human review. Verdicts come from held out requests, and each further verdict on the same held out set multiplies its p value by the number of verdicts given.
